'''Tabekoten Shrine''' (たべこてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kawabe, Gifu|arz|كوابه|ceb|Kawabe-chō|es|Kawabe (Gifu)|fa|کاوابه، گیفو|fr|Kawabe|it|Kawabe|ja|川辺町|ko|가와베정|ms|Kawabe, Gifu|my|ခါဝဘဲမြို့၊ ဂိဖု|pl|Kawabe (Gifu)|ru|Кавабе|tl|Kawabe, Gifu|tr|Kawabe|uk|Кавабе|ur|کاوا بے، گیفو|uz|Kavabe (Gifu)|zh|川邊町|qid=Q1203748}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|ceb|Kamo-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Gifu-ken)|es|Distrito de Kamo (Gifu)|fr|District de Kamo (Gifu)|id|Distrik Kamo, Gifu|it|Distretto di Kamo (Gifu)|ja|加茂郡|ko|가모군 (기후현)|pl|Powiat Kamo|pt|Distrito de Kamo|th|อำเภอคาโมะ|uk|Повіт Камо (Ґіфу)|vi|Kamo (quận)|zh|加茂郡|qid=Q1348656}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}.

It is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for Tabe Shrine, a shikinaisha of Kamo District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}. Another theory identifies Tabe Shrine with {{ill|Tabe Shrine|Q11444532|qid=Q11444532}} in the same town. Its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was village shrine.

The annual festival on the second Saturday and Sunday of April is called the Tabekoten Shrine Festival, in which two {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} are pulled.

=== Overview ===
The founding date is unknown. It is said to have formerly been called Tabe Shrine and Tabekotenjin, and later to have merged Sugawara no Michizane.

In the Edo period, it was said to be the village guardian shrine and general shrine of Kawabe for Kawabe village, Ishigami village, Kashio village, and Tochii village (now the west-bank area of the {{ill|Hida River|Q3366160|qid=Q3366160}} in Kawabe). Since Meiji, it has been the village guardian shrine of Nakakawabe and Nishitochii.

=== Tabekoten Shrine Festival ===
*A festival transmitted since the Edo period. Two floats are pulled from Tochii Shrine to Tabekoten Shrine, and lion dance is dedicated in the precincts.
*At 6:00 a.m. on Sunday, the “sake-buying rite” is held. Early in the morning, a parishioner wearing the mask of “Haiō,” messenger of Tenjin, goes with the lion to a sake brewery and buys sake to offer to Tenjin.
*This rite is performed entirely as {{ill|Mime|Q39818|qid=Q39818}}.
*Haiō is said either to be {{ill|Emperor Gaozong of Tang|Q9703|qid=Q9703}} of {{ill|Han dynasty|Q7209|qid=Q7209}} or another name of a Han warrior, but details are unknown. Haiō appears wearing a mask (close to a {{ill|Tengu|Q742360|qid=Q742360}} mask but with a less prominent nose) wrapped with a shimenawa-like band. This resembles the fly-chasing man in the annual festival of {{ill|Abushina Shrine|ja|阿夫志奈神社|qid=Q11657364}}, also in Kawabe, said to represent {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}.

=== Cultural properties ===
